questions.stem: The game in which the term 'LBW' is used is:
questions.explanation: LBW = Leg Before Wicket — a method of dismissal in cricket.

options.option_text: India has no officially declared National Sport

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports confirmed in 2012 (RTI reply) that India has NOT officially declared any sport as its National Sport. Hockey is commonly believed to be, but no government notification exists.

questions.stem: The number of players in a KABADDI team on the court at any time is:
questions.explanation: Kabaddi — 7 players per side on court (out of 12 in squad). Other sports headcount: football 11; hockey 11; volleyball 6; basketball 5; kho-kho 9 (12 squad); water polo 7; rugby 15.

questions.stem: NEERAJ CHOPRA is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra (Haryana) — javelin gold at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (8 Aug 2021) with 87.58 m. India's first-ever Olympic gold in athletics, second-ever individual Olympic gold (after Abhinav Bindra 2008). World Athletics Championships gold 2023 (Budapest, 88.17 m). Paris 2024 Olympic silver.

questions.stem: Consider the following about INDIAN CRICKET. 1. India won its first Cricket World Cup (ODI) in 1983 under Kapil Dev. 2. India won the ICC T20 World Cup in 2007 under MS Dhoni. 3. India won the ICC Cricket World Cup (ODI) in 2011 under MS Dhoni. 4. India won the World Test Championship Final in 2021 (inaugural cycle). Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — NEW ZEALAND won the inaugural World Test Championship Final (June 2021, Southampton) defeating India. India had reached the final. The WTC 2023 final at The Oval was won by AUSTRALIA (beating India again). Statements 1-3 are correct.

questions.stem: Match the sport with its trophy. A. Hockey (World Cup, FIH). B. Football (World Cup, FIFA). C. Cricket (ODI World Cup). D. Tennis (oldest Grand Slam). List-II: 1. FIFA World Cup Trophy. 2. ICC Cricket World Cup Trophy. 3. Wimbledon. 4. FIH World Cup (Hockey) trophy.
questions.explanation: Simple pairing. Wimbledon (1877) is the oldest of the four Grand Slams (the others: Australian Open 1905, French Open 1891, US Open 1881 — note US Open's first iteration predates AO/FO but Wimbledon remains oldest).
